turns.q: How do I use it correctly to get the best result?
turns.replyTail:
the water droplet test by sprinkling a little water into the pan. If the droplets form rolling beads, your pan is at the right temperature and you can add a bit of fat.

Avoid cooking on high heat, as our 3-ply stainless steel conducts and retains heat extremely well. For meat, do not try to move it right away when it touches the pan, as it will naturally release once the crust forms.

Finally, deglaze your pan with lukewarm water right after cooking to easily lift any food residue 🙂

10:47 AM
turns.replyText:
10:46 AM. You said:

How do I use it correctly to get the best result?

10:46 AM
10:47 AM. Lucas says:
Lucas

Adam, cooking with stainless steel is simple once you follow a few easy steps. First, always preheat your pan empty for two minutes on medium heat.

Next, perform the water droplet test by sprinkling a little water into the pan. If the droplets form rolling beads, your pan is at the right temperature and you can add a bit of fat.

Avoid cooking on high heat, as our 3-ply stainless steel conducts and retains heat extremely well. For meat, do not try to move it right away when it touches the pan, as it will naturally release once the crust forms.

Finally, deglaze your pan with lukewarm water right after cooking to easily lift any food residue 🙂
